items.title: Remote LSP transport and identity are explicit
items.statement: Remote LSP uses stdio over SSH, operates directly on the remote filesystem, and preserves a host-scoped remote project identity without a hidden local mirror.

evidence.exact_quote: - transport is stdio over SSH; the remote LSP server stdin/stdout are tunneled through the SSH connection rather than exposed by port forwarding
- remote LSP uses the remote filesystem directly; there is no hidden local sync or mirror for LSP operations

- The stale local-only phrase `(server_id, root)` is retained only as migration contrast. Live LSP attach/session keys are `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`, and remote documents use host-scoped `/path-mapping` so a file-local URI on host A cannot collide with the same path on host B.

items.title: SSH loss drives bounded degraded recovery
items.statement: An SSH disconnect degrades every LSP server multiplexed on that connection, attempts reconnect, reinitializes servers, and replays pending requests only when safe; the SSH owner permits one bounded automatic retry before explicit Reconnect.

evidence.exact_quote: - if SSH disconnects, all remote LSP servers on that connection are marked `degraded`, reconnect is attempted, servers are re-initialized, and pending requests are replayed when safe

- Remote LSP is part of the `remote-mode-project` model, not a `remote-edit-only` feature and not a broad-sweep local editor patch. This seam is research-locked for implementation transfer. `GitHub_Integration.md §C` is the SSH `/ownership` anchor for `/edit/test/remove`, validation `/auth/host-key`, add-existing-project, remote terminal, remote agents, remote `/providers`, and remote runtime execution. `GitHub_Integration.md §C.3-C.4` / `C.3-C.4` is the operational reconnect authority: keep the 30s keepalive, allow one bounded auto-retry (`one-auto-retry` in older notes), then require explicit `Reconnect`.

items.title: Lifecycle state taxonomy conflicts with the transition table
items.statement: The canonical user/state list names `RestartBackoff`, `ShuttingDown`, and `Stopped`, while the immediately following state chain and table use `stopping` and `crashed` and omit `RestartBackoff`. The mapping between user projection states and internal transition states is not specified, so implementations can expose or persist incompatible state values.
items.impact: State persistence, GUI status, restart behavior, and consumers of lifecycle_state can disagree on valid states and transitions.
items.builder_discretion: An implementer must invent whether `crashed` maps to `RestartBackoff`, whether `stopping` maps to `ShuttingDown`, and which vocabulary is serialized or user-visible.

evidence.exact_quote: Canonical user/state names are `Starting`, `Initializing`, `Ready`, `RestartBackoff`, `Degraded`, `ShuttingDown`, and `Stopped`. Only `Ready` emits normal feature traffic; `Starting` and `Initializing` may queue sync work, `RestartBackoff` exposes countdown plus last error, and `Degraded` can mean paused recovery or diagnostics-only / diagnostics-only attachment. Each document is attached once per session, including virtual-doc buffers, and `didClose` is emitted when the final attachment for that `(session, uri)` disappears. The session/model boundary records `/URI` identity so virtual-doc and real-file URI values do not collide.
States: `stopped → starting → initializing → ready → degraded → stopping → crashed`

| any | crashed | server process dies unexpectedly | log error, attempt restart |
| crashed | starting | auto-restart (max 3 attempts, backoff 2s/4s/8s) | respawn |
| crashed | stopped | restart limit exceeded | show error, require manual restart |

items.title: Stale-response retry policy is contradictory
items.statement: The normative stale-response policy forbids automatic re-request, but the implementation checklist permits discard or re-request. This changes observable request volume and whether a stale user action can produce a later result without explicit repetition.
items.impact: Different implementations can either silently retry stale requests or require the user to repeat the action, producing inconsistent UX and server load.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must choose which contradictory stale-response instruction wins.

evidence.exact_quote: **Stale response policy:** When a response arrives for a document-scoped request (hover, completion, definition, references, signatureHelp), the client must check whether the document version has changed since the request was sent. Store the document version (from `DocumentState.version` for that URI) at request time; when the response is received, compare to the current `DocumentState.version`. If the current version is **greater** than the version at request time, **discard** the response (do not show tooltip, do not apply completion, do not navigate). Optionally match by request id so only the correct response is discarded. **Do not** automatically re-request; the user can repeat the action (e.g. hover again, trigger completion again) to get a fresh result. For workspace-level requests (e.g. workspace/symbol), version check is per relevant document or omit if no single document applies.
- [ ] Request timeout and cancellation; discard or re-request on stale document version. Per-server enable/disable: honor lsp.<id>.disabled and lsp: false. Settings > LSP per FinalGUISpec §7.4.2.

items.title: Document authority and save ordering are explicit
items.statement: LspSupervisor and DocumentStore form the supervision boundary, all editor and virtual-document surfaces consume the same authoritative buffer and pending-sync state, and didSave follows a successful shared-store save for the current version.

evidence.exact_quote: The `/supervision` boundary is `LspSupervisor` plus `DocumentStore`: `/document-pane` surfaces, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, and `/revert` all consume the same authoritative buffer and pending-sync state. LSP never reads a second document authority for an open file, and `didSave` is emitted only after the shared document store records a successful save for the current version.
- A successful save may emit `didSave` for the current document version/content state. Failed save does not emit `didSave`, and stale-result handling must not make the UI look saved or synchronized.

items.title: URI, version, request generation, and position encoding share one freshness contract
items.statement: Document-scoped responses apply only to the same live session epoch, URI, current document version, and latest request class; canonical host-scoped DocumentUri identity and centralized negotiated position conversion prevent collisions and hand-rolled code-unit math.

evidence.exact_quote: Document identity, freshness, and `/position` conversion are one contract. Before `didClose`, PM cancels in-flight document-scoped requests for `(session, uri)` and clears diagnostics per `(server/session, uri)`. Each document-scoped request carries `session_epoch`, `uri`, `document_version`, and `request_generation` or an equivalent latest-of-class marker; responses apply only for the same live session epoch, same URI, matching current document version, and latest relevant request class. Late replies are discarded in UX but remain visible in trace `/logs`.

At open time, PM creates one canonical `DocumentUri` per document/host and reuses it consistently. The same physical file must not gain duplicate identities through case, `/slash/drive-letter`, URI spelling, `(session, uri)` pairing, or `/path/position` conversion differences. UI/editor surfaces stay 1-based where already planned; the LSP boundary remains 0-based and uses one position-mapper / position-mapping service backed by `DocumentStore`. `capabilities.positionEncoding` and `position_encoding` are negotiated per session; PM uses compatibility-first position-encoding, keeps UTF-16 as the guaranteed baseline, may prefer `utf-8` only after compatibility proof, and must not hard-code UTF assumptions into hover, `/completion/diagnostics/rename`, diagnostics, rename, or formatting handlers. Conversion uses fast per-line helpers/cache so multi-server correctness, remote `/SSH`, and performance tuning stay protocol-safe.

LSP coordinates use the protocol's code-unit conventions at the boundary; the centralized conversion layer records whether a server uses UTF-16 code-unit offsets, another negotiated encoding, or compatibility fallback, so individual feature handlers never hand-roll code-unit math.

items.title: Sync barriers and re-baselining are specified
items.statement: Per-session sync is FIFO, document requests wait for Ready and flushed sync, soft requests coalesce by request class, and loss of incremental confidence escalates from whole-document replacement to session restart and attached-document replay.

evidence.exact_quote: - Sync events are FIFO per session. A document-scoped request must not leave the queue until the target session is `Ready`, the prior `didOpen`/`didChange` work for that document in that session has flushed, and the document is no longer in pending-sync state.

- `didChange` debounce is resetting `/coalescing`, not fixed-window batching. All mutations since the last sent sync for that session/doc become one batch; if incremental confidence is lost, send a whole-document replacement to re-baseline; if confidence is still not trustworthy, restart the session and replay currently attached docs.

items.title: GUI consumers and degraded-state copy are defined
items.statement: Remote GUI surfaces expose capability, editor state, and degraded copy while consuming the SSH owner contract; diagnostics project to the Problems tab and gutter, and status and fallback behavior are acceptance-tested.

evidence.exact_quote: - `Settings > SSH` and GUI remote-editor surfaces expose remote capability, editor-state, and degraded copy, but they consume the SSH owner contract instead of redefining it. `file-editor`, FileManager, Terminal, Source Control, provider, `/debug`, and `/runtime` surfaces share the same `/read-only/offline/refresh`, `/offline/degraded`, `/enabled`, and unavailable vocabulary.
3. **Server sends publishDiagnostics** → Client receives → Update DiagnosticsCache for that URI → Notify UI (main thread) → Problems tab and gutter update.

| **9. Status and fallback** | LSP status in status bar; per-server enable/disable; fallback to heuristic when no server; optional install hint. | Status bar shows server state; disabling server stops LSP for that language; heuristic outline used when LSP off. |

items.title: Configuration storage alternatives conflict with the later locked location
items.statement: The config section allows app storage in redb or YAML and project overrides in a file or redb, while the later decision section fixes app configuration under `config.lsp` and project overrides at `.puppet-master/lsp.json`. The document does not explicitly retire the earlier alternatives.
items.impact: Builders can persist equivalent settings in different stores, producing divergent precedence, migration, and interoperability behavior.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must infer whether the later location supersedes all earlier storage alternatives and whether any redb project-key/YAML compatibility path remains.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Storage:** App-level in **redb** (or existing config YAML) under a key like `config.lsp`. Project-level override: optional file in project root (e.g. `.puppet-master/lsp.json`) or key under project id in redb.
App-level configuration lives under `config.lsp`.
Project overrides live at `.puppet-master/lsp.json`.

items.title: workspaceFolders overflow is declared deterministic without a selection order
items.statement: The policy caps workspace folders at ten open-document roots and requires deterministic exclusion with evidence, but it does not define which roots win when more than ten qualify.
items.impact: Different root-ordering choices can attach different folders to an LSP session and change diagnostics, symbols, and resource usage.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must invent a stable ordering or priority rule for overflow roots.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Recommendation:** At initialize, send **only roots that have at least one open document**, capped at **10** roots. If user has no open files, send project root if single-root, else empty list. Reduces startup cost and memory; document in implementation guide. Re-initialize not required when opening a file in a new root; the matching host-aware server session handles that.
Only roots containing at least one open document are included, up to the cap above. Overflow roots are excluded deterministically and MUST be visible in logs/evidence when exclusion affects behavior.

items.title: Virtual-document identity, attachment, and lifecycle are mostly explicit
items.statement: Chat code blocks use non-disk virtual URIs, attach to the effective host-aware language server session, open on LSP need, close on eviction/view closure, and never receive didChange because block instances are immutable.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Creation:** When the user focuses or hovers over a code block in a Chat message that has a known language id and the project has an LSP server for that language, create a virtual document: assign a URI, set content to the block text, and attach it to the **server for that language and the effective host/root identity for the current project context** (same session that would handle a real file with that extension). If the block maps to a real project file (e.g. "snippet from src/main.rs"), use the real file URI instead and do not create a virtual doc.

- **Contract for implementer:** (1) Virtual URI never points to disk; (2) one virtual doc per code block instance (same block in UI = same opaque_id); (3) didOpen is sent when the block needs LSP (hover/definition); (4) didClose is sent when the block is evicted or the view is closed; (5) hover/definition requests for that block use the virtual URI and the same `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)` as for that language in the current project context.

items.title: The no-discretion claim is contradicted by unresolved runtime choices
items.statement: The window claims no core runtime behavior remains implementation-defined, yet it leaves the client crate open, permits alternative virtual-document eviction strategies and cache sizes, and uses optional behavior within the core contract.
items.impact: Independent builders can make materially different lifecycle, resource, and dependency choices while all claiming conformance.
items.builder_discretion: Choice of LSP client, virtual-document idle eviction, recent-document retention, and some request behavior remains delegated to the implementer.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Dependencies:** `lsp-types`, chosen LSP client crate (e.g. `lsp-client` or `async_lsp_client`), `tokio` for async. No need for tower-lsp unless implementing a server.

- **Lifecycle:** Send `textDocument/didOpen` when the virtual document is "opened" (e.g. when the user first hovers or requests definition in that block). Send `textDocument/didClose` when the block is no longer needed: when the user scrolls away from that message, when the message is collapsed, or when the Chat view is closed; or after T seconds idle (e.g. 300 s) if implementing eviction by timeout. Optionally retain a bounded set of recently used virtual docs (e.g. last 5) to avoid repeated didOpen/didClose on quick hover. Do not send `didChange` for virtual docs (blocks are immutable); if the user edits the message and the block content changes, treat as a new block (new opaque_id) and close the old virtual doc.
No core runtime LSP behavior remains implementation-defined after this section.

items.title: ServerSpec and catalog precedence establish registry authority
items.statement: ServerSpec is the canonical machine-friendly record, the effective catalog is a deduplicated union with overlays, generated prose is non-authoritative, and effective resolution follows catalog, global override, project override, then runtime availability.

evidence.exact_quote: `ServerSpec` is the canonical machine-friendly catalog record for both built-in and custom servers.

- the effective support catalog is the deduped union of Microsoft implementor data, OpenCode catalog data, and Puppet Master overlay metadata
- user enable/disable and custom-server settings layer on top of the catalog instead of replacing it
- derived prose tables and `/readable` `/settings/docs` views may be generated from this support-catalog registry, but this structure remains the SSOT and prevents the large union catalog from becoming duplicate-prone prose
- Support scope and support classification stay separate in the `/catalog`: supported-by-registry, default-managed, toolchain-bound `/manual`, experimental `/degraded`, and deprecated or `/replaced` are classification outcomes layered over stable `server_id` identity, not reasons to fork the catalog SSOT. Effective resolution order is catalog base entry, global override, project override, then runtime availability and `/effective-state` evaluation.

items.title: Acceptance phase taxonomy is internally inconsistent
items.statement: The implementation table defines ten numbered phases, but the single implementation-ready checklist declares done conditions for only Phases 1-4 and assigns broader feature groupings to those numbers. The document does not map the ten-phase table to the four-phase checklist or state which phase taxonomy governs completion.
items.impact: Progress reporting and completion gates can mark different scopes complete under the same phase number.
items.builder_discretion: The builder or verifier must invent a mapping between the ten implementation phases and four checklist phases.

evidence.exact_quote:
| Phase | Deliverables | Acceptance criteria |
|-------|--------------|---------------------|
| **1. Foundation** | LSP client crate integrated; server registry (in-memory); config loading (lsp.* from redb/config). | App starts; config can disable LSP globally; registry returns server id by extension. |
| **2. Spawn and lifecycle** | Spawn server process per (id, root); stdio transport; initialize handshake; shutdown/exit on close. | Opening a `.rs` file (with rust-analyzer in PATH) spawns one process; closing all files in that root shuts down server. |
| **3. Document sync** | didOpen, didChange (debounced), didClose, didSave; version tracking; incremental sync when server supports. | Editing file sends didChange after debounce; version increments; no flood of messages. |
| **4. Diagnostics** | Subscribe to publishDiagnostics; store per URI; expose to UI. | Problems tab shows errors/warnings for open files; gutter shows markers; click opens file at line. |
| **5. Hover and completion** | textDocument/hover and textDocument/completion; timeout and cancel; tooltip and completion list in editor. | Hover shows type/docs; completion list appears on trigger; stale responses discarded. |
| **6. Navigation** | documentSymbol, textDocument/definition (and references); breadcrumbs and go-to-symbol use LSP when available. | Breadcrumbs reflect LSP outline; go to symbol/definition jump to correct location. |
| **7. Inlay hints, semantic tokens, signature help** | inlayHint, semanticTokens, signatureHelp; render in editor. | Inlay hints and signature help visible; semantic highlighting improves colors when supported. |
| **8. Code actions and code lens** | codeAction (context menu/lightbulb), codeLens; apply via workspace/applyEdit through FileSafe. | Quick fixes appear and apply correctly; code lens links invoke. |
| **9. Status and fallback** | LSP status in status bar; per-server enable/disable; fallback to heuristic when no server; optional install hint. | Status bar shows server state; disabling server stops LSP for that language; heuristic outline used when LSP off. |
| **10. LLM diagnostics** | Include current diagnostics in Assistant/Interview context. | Agent receives diagnostic list for relevant files when composing context. |

**Acceptance (done when):** Each Phase 1-4 item is done when: (1) **Prerequisites:** App builds with lsp-types + chosen client crate; config schema and keys exist in storage. (2) **Phase 1:** Opening a file with a matching server spawns the server; diagnostics appear in Problems tab and gutter; hover and completion work with timeout/stale discard; status bar shows server state. (3) **Phase 2:** Go to definition, Find references, Rename, Format work; code actions apply via FileSafe; code lens invokes; Settings > LSP lists all servers and custom entries with validation. (4) **Phase 3:** Assistant/Interview context includes diagnostic summary (capped 10 files, 50 diagnostics); @ symbol includes LSP workspace/symbol; code blocks in Chat support hover and click-to-definition; Problems link in Chat footer opens Problems tab. (5) **Phase 4:** Optional gate, evidence snapshot, subagent bias, and Chat/Interview enhancements implemented per §9.1 or explicitly deferred and documented.

items.title: Resource-limit enforcement and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The window defines a configurable 512MB default memory maximum and a 30-second single-request CPU maximum, but gives no measurement boundary, enforcement mechanism, over-limit state transition, user-facing reason, or recovery action.
items.impact: Implementations can kill, throttle, degrade, or ignore over-limit servers differently, affecting reliability and observability.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must invent how limits are measured and enforced and how a session recovers after exceeding them.

evidence.exact_quote:
Resource limits:
- max memory per server is configurable, default `512MB`
- max CPU time for a single request is `30s`

items.title: Mutation authority and partial-failure reporting stay with FileSafe
items.statement: Preview-worthy and multi-file LSP mutations use FileSafe confirmation, partial failures report per-file results, unavailable targets show explicit reasons, and LSP cannot bypass safety, policy, or blocked-state reporting.

evidence.exact_quote: - Remote mutation and availability modes are user-visible. Preview-worthy rename, multi-file code-action, and broad format operations require the same safe preview `/confirmation` path as other FileSafe edits; partial workspace-edit failure reports per-file results, and read-only, locked, unavailable, or `/degraded` targets fail with explicit reason copy. Remote effective modes include `full_remote_lsp`, `degraded_remote_diagnostics_only`, and `remote_edit_no_lsp`; unsupported local-LSP-on-remote-paths behavior must not masquerade as `on-remote-paths` correctness.

`workspace/applyEdit`, rename, and code-action application use the same FileSafe-backed apply-edit path as other agent mutations.
- multi-file edits are treated as multi-file mutations
- destructive edits use the same safety and approval rules as any other file mutation path
- LSP does not bypass FileSafe, tool policy, or blocked-state reporting

items.title: SSH credential storage is explicitly excluded from config
items.statement: Remote LSP credentials remain in system keychain or agent flows and are not stored in configuration.

evidence.exact_quote: - Remote paths preserve the user-visible SSH authority: examples such as `user@host:/path/to/project` and `/path/to/project` describe the same remote project identity, not a local mirror. Remote LSP is MVP for remote edit intelligence and diagnostics, but remote run/debug remains outside FileManager's edit contract unless another runtime owner enables it. On connection-loss, LSP state follows the FileManager/GUI pattern: show `Connection lost`, offer `Reconnect` or `Work offline (cached files only)` when a validated cache exists, keep credentials in system keychain/agent flows rather than config, and expose keep-alive/backoff state through `ssh_connections` compatibility lineage or the current SSH remote profile model.

items.title: Diagnostic and trace payload privacy is not defined in this window
items.statement: The contract sends current diagnostics into Assistant/Interview context and retains late replies in trace logs, but this window does not specify redaction, retention, access control, or user-visible disclosure for source paths, messages, symbols, or reply payloads.
items.impact: Diagnostics and LSP replies can contain project paths or source-derived content and may propagate to model context or persistent logs without a local policy in this contract.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must rely on an unstated external privacy/logging policy or invent filtering and retention behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: Document identity, freshness, and `/position` conversion are one contract. Before `didClose`, PM cancels in-flight document-scoped requests for `(session, uri)` and clears diagnostics per `(server/session, uri)`. Each document-scoped request carries `session_epoch`, `uri`, `document_version`, and `request_generation` or an equivalent latest-of-class marker; responses apply only for the same live session epoch, same URI, matching current document version, and latest relevant request class. Late replies are discarded in UX but remain visible in trace `/logs`.

- [ ] **Diagnostics in Assistant context:** When building context for next Assistant/Interview turn, include summary of current LSP diagnostics (file, line, message, severity, source) for project or @'d/recently edited files.

items.title: Primary message inputs, outputs, and UI-thread propagation are explicit
items.statement: The message flow specifies open/edit/diagnostics/hover/completion inputs and outputs; all protocol I/O runs asynchronously and UI updates are marshaled to the Slint event loop without blocking it.

evidence.exact_quote:
1. **User opens file** → Editor loads buffer → Resolve (path → extension → server id → effective host/root identity) → If server not running for `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`, spawn process → Initialize handshake → Send `didOpen` with content + version.
2. **User edits** → Buffer content changes → Increment version; **debounce** (e.g. 100 ms) → Send `didChange` (incremental if supported) with version.
3. **Server sends publishDiagnostics** → Client receives → Update DiagnosticsCache for that URI → Notify UI (main thread) → Problems tab and gutter update.
4. **User hovers** → Editor sends (uri, position) → Client sends `textDocument/hover` (with timeout) → On response, check document version; if stale, discard → Show tooltip.
5. **User triggers completion** → Client sends `textDocument/completion` with context → On response, filter/discard if stale → Show list; on select, apply and optionally `completionItem/resolve`.
All LSP I/O on **async task** (tokio); route UI updates to the Slint event loop (e.g. via `slint::invoke_from_event_loop` or `Weak::upgrade_in_event_loop`). Never block UI on LSP.

items.title: Compatibility alias and merge precedence are defined
items.statement: The canonical namespace is `lsp.servers.<id>.*`, the legacy disabled alias maps to it, and the locked merge rules define scalar, object, array, inheritance, and server-specific precedence behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Keys:** `lsp.enabled` (bool, default true), `lsp.servers.<id>.disabled` (bool), `lsp.servers.<id>.command` (string array), `lsp.servers.<id>.extensions` (string array), `lsp.servers.<id>.env` (object), `lsp.servers.<id>.initialization` (object). **Decision:** Config namespace is `lsp.servers.<id>.*`; support legacy alias `lsp.<id>.disabled` (read/write maps to `lsp.servers.<id>.disabled`). Align with OpenCode schema for compatibility.

Merge rules:
- scalar keys override
- object keys override by nested key
- arrays replace rather than merge
- absent keys inherit
- server-specific settings resolve by server id first, then by language/filetype mapping only when no explicit server-id override exists

dimension_assessments.summary: Transport, message flow, remote behavior, async execution, sync ordering, stale handling, and fallback behavior are substantially specified, with the stale retry contradiction separately recorded.
Local/remote edit intelligence, diagnostics, navigation, completion, code actions, virtual documents, Chat consumption, and fallback capabilities are enumerated.
The message flow identifies buffer, URI, version, position, diagnostics, completion, hover, and UI projection inputs and outputs.
Document, URI, mutation, registry, and sync contracts are strong, but stale-response behavior and configuration authority contain direct conflicts.
Transitions and crash backoff are enumerated, but canonical projection states do not align with the state chain and transition-table vocabulary.
SSH ownership, FileSafe mutation authority, DocumentStore buffer authority, and ServerSpec catalog authority are explicitly assigned.
LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore own supervision and buffer truth; Problems owns diagnostic merging; SSH and FileSafe retain their respective remote and mutation contracts.
Editor, Problems, gutter, Settings, Source Control, Search, Assistant/Interview, Chat, and status surfaces have defined LSP projections or consumption boundaries.
Visible degraded copy, status values, Problems/gutter updates, hover/completion UI, Settings controls, and Chat links are specified.
SSH reconnect, crash restart, sync re-baselining, stale discard, offline states, and partial edit failure are covered; resource-limit breach handling is not.
Credential storage is safely constrained, but diagnostic/model-context and trace-log payload privacy, retention, and redaction are not defined in this window.
Diagnostics, capabilities, stale state, remote availability, buffer state, and LSP results have explicit propagation into UI and adjacent consumers.
Backoff, keepalive, manual restart, trace logs, async execution, timeout defaults, and evidence visibility are specified, but resource-limit enforcement is not operationally closed.
Remote timeout multiplication, debounce, async nonblocking I/O, fast position caches, workspace-root caps, and resource defaults are present; overflow ordering and limit enforcement remain open.

Host-aware identity, UTF-16 baseline, OpenCode-aligned keys, legacy disabled alias, and catalog classification are defined, but storage compatibility is ambiguous because earlier alternatives are not explicitly retired.
Feature-level observable criteria exist, but the ten-phase table and four-phase implementation checklist use incompatible phase numbering and scope.

Client choice, virtual-document eviction/cache behavior, overflow root ordering, storage compatibility, state mapping, resource enforcement, and stale retry behavior require builder judgment despite a no-discretion claim.

Material unknowns remain in lifecycle vocabulary, stale retries, config storage, root overflow ordering, phase mapping, resource-limit behavior, privacy handling, and the scope of claimed implementation closure.
